reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1-E3 show that Cr2O3 did not form on a similar HEA under oxidation conditions, contradicting the premise of a protective Cr2O3 scale. E4 discusses HEA-reinforced composites but not oxide scales or pre-oxidation effects. E5 mentions in-situ oxide film formation reducing friction, but this is a dynamic process during wear, not a controlled pre-oxidation treatment, and does not address wear rate or deformation patterns.
premises: Pre-oxidation at ~700°C forms a continuous, adherent, ultrathin Cr2O3/spinel scale on FeNiCrCoCu HEA
Cr2O3 scale acts as a protective barrier against oxidation and diffusion
Oxide scale reduces adhesive metal-metal contact and friction
Oxide scale redistributes shear stresses, limiting plastic deformation and microcracking
Pre-oxidized coating shows lower wear rate and less severe deformation than untreated coating at 600–700°C
